recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes should only be made if FHIR-I wants new or stronger CapabilityStatement conformance language, which would be a separate work-group decision rather than remaining work for FHIR-42971.
issue_request: FHIR-42971 was Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core HTTP after a 2023-10-30 FHIR-I 9-0-0 vote. It asked to remove text saying a server default timezone SHOULD be returned in the HTTP Date response header and to add documentation that a server's time zone should be discoverable using the timezone extension on CapabilityStatement.meta.
initial_application: Gino Canessa's Jira-tagged implementation commits b811010c8b and 8e74a757dd removed the Date-header timezone sentence from source/http.html, added a Timezone Discovery section to source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-notes.xml, and made a minor wording adjustment. Those substantive changes remain in current source.
additional_context: The triggering Zulip thread explains that HTTP Date values are UTC/GMT and cannot carry a local timezone. FHIR-I minutes from 2023-10-30 record the work-group rationale to use the timezone extension on CapabilityStatement.meta. The current FHIR Extension Pack timezone StructureDefinition allows Meta as a context, so the core source's extension reference is consistent with the external definition. Historical FHIR-16434 explains why the now-invalid sentence had previously been moved to the HTTP return-content section.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because no current core source edit is needed. source/http.html no longer contains the invalid guidance, and source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-notes.xml already documents server default timezone discovery through the timezone code extension on CapabilityStatement.meta.
